title: linkshare: a small social network for links

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Picture a feed where friends drop the articles they're reading. You hover over a title, and a preview card pops up with the page, the votes and the comments. That's linkshare.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Antoine. It's a Ruby on Rails app, version 4.1. He started from an online tutorial, then added his own pieces: a link previewer, an admin page and more ways for members to interact.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So what can a member actually do?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sign up with a name and an avatar picture, then post a link with a title and a description. The same form can carry a file instead of a link, so people can share documents too.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the preview card, where does that come from?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: From a service called Embedly. The feed marks each link as an Embedly card, and a small script in the browser asks Embedly to draw the preview. The app doesn't have to fetch and parse the page itself.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Clever. What about the social part, the votes and comments?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Every link has a like and a dislike button, handled by a Rails voting library. Comments hang off each link, so the discussion stays next to the thing being discussed.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And when the feed gets long?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It shows five links per page, and there's a search that matches link titles or member names. Member cards even show a little online indicator.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Someone has to keep it tidy, though.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the admin side. Accounts have an admin flag, and a ready-made admin panel lives under slash admin, where an administrator can manage links, comments and users.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So in one small project you get accounts, uploads, previews, voting, comments, search and moderation.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly, a full tour of a classic server-rendered Rails app. The written page walks through the routes, the data model and the steps to run it.
